messages:
Sophie: Hey — customer (acct 3245) reports their streaming responses drop cleanly after ~30s with no error. request_id=rcq_9a8b7c6d, model=redwood-alpha, region=us-west-2. Can we get a minimal curl repro template + which headers/logs to collect?

Mike: thanks. first step: we need a cURL that reproduces the exact request shape (headers, method, body) and the raw response headers. Ask them to run with --no-buffer and a header dump. Example I sent below.

Lina: also confirm if they go through a corporate proxy or load balancer. proxies often terminate SSE or chunked streams early. If proxy, ask for proxy env vars and `curl -v` output.

Alex: sample command I usually give customers — replace <TOKEN> <URL> and remove sensitive data before sending back:

```
curl -v --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","input":"hello"}' "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/stream"
```

Mike: add these flags to capture everything we need: `--dump-header headers.txt --trace-ascii curl.trace --raw`. That gives response headers and a byte-for-byte trace. Full cmd:

```
curl --no-buffer --http1.1 --dump-header headers.txt --trace-ascii curl.trace --raw -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","input":"hi"}' "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/stream"
```

Dan: if they can run tcpdump/pcap that helps too (filter by host). Otherwise curl.trace + headers.txt + the request_id from the final connection is usually enough. Ask them to redaction-mask tokens before uploading.

Sophie: good. Also ask them to run a short loop to see if it's deterministic: 10 requests with a 5s sleep and attach the run output, mention which attempts dropped.

Lina: note about timeouts: some proxies close idle streams after default keepalive ~30s. To prove it's not server-side, have them run the same curl against `https://httpbin.org/stream/100` and compare behavior. If httpbin also cuts, it's likely client/proxy.

Alex: small troubleshooting curl variants to try (include in instructions):
- force HTTP/1.1 `--http1.1`
- disable proxy `--noproxy "*"` or set `-x ""`
- add `--no-keepalive` and `--keepalive-time 20`
- capture TLS debug `--trace-ascii tls.trace`

Sophie: can you paste a short masked trace when you get it. Also include the full top-level response headers.txt and the curl.trace.

Mike: if the trace shows `Connection: keep-alive` then server kept it, look for `FIN`/`RST` in tcpdump. If we see `HTTP/1.1 200` then a normal SSE payload, we want to see if the client sends a FIN.

dev-bot: DEBUG-CHECKLIST: Please include — request_id, region, model, exact curl cmd, headers.txt, curl.trace, system clock skew, proxy env vars, sample client app logs. (auto message)

Sophie: I'll send this checklist to the customer and ask them to run the two curl commands (normal + with traces). I'll request a single .zip with files and a short note on which attempt dropped.

Lina: remind them to redact tokens and API keys; they can replace with `<REDACTED>` — we only need traces.

Alex: if they prefer we can provide a tiny repro script that retries and prints timestamps per chunk — that helps correlate with network captures. I can paste one if needed.

Sophie: perfect. I'll follow up here with the bundle once they upload. Thanks all :pray:
